title: file input: multipart support, size limits, and content-type validation for OpenAI-compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add multipart/form-data file input support for OpenAI-compat endpoints; enforce per-file and aggregate payload limits; stricter content-type validation and improved error messages
description:
Context: Several customers and integration tests surfaced inconsistencies between Redwood's file input handling and the OpenAI compatibility layer. In particular: multipart/form-data uploads were accepted but not validated consistently, large payloads caused unexpected runtime errors in the API gateway, and content-type handling allowed ambiguous types leading to downstream parsing failures. This PR implements end-to-end fixes for the OpenAI-compat file input surface.

Summary of changes: implemented robust multipart parsing for the openai-compat endpoints; added per-file size limit (configurable) and aggregate payload limit with clear 413 responses; strengthened Content-Type validation (reject unsupported or ambiguous types with 415); added deterministic content-sniffing fallback for missing content-type; surfaced user-friendly error payloads matching OpenAI compat schema; added extensive unit and integration tests; updated API docs and error docs.

Motivation: Reduce silent failures and inconsistent behavior when customers upload files (tool inputs, function-call payloads, embeddings attachments). These fixes reduce incident noise, improve compatibility for third-party SDKs, and make error modes explicit. See ENG-4289 for background and test vectors.

Checklist:
- [x] multipart/form-data parsing implemented for openai-compat endpoints
- [x] per-file and total payload limits enforced, configurable via config/file_upload_limits
- [x] content-type validation + content-sniffing fallback
- [x] deterministic, OpenAI-compat error responses (413/415/400)
- [x] unit tests for parser, validator, and limiter
- [x] integration tests exercising SDK uploads
- [x] docs and release notes updated

Rollout plan: feature behind a flag openai_compat_file_validation by default enabled for new clusters; staged rollout to dedicated customers and Canary environment for 48h; monitor error rates and request latency. Auto-roll back if upload error spike > 2% or 95th latency regressions > 20%.

Notes on backwards compatibility: Default behavior preserves existing upload endpoints for non-openai-compat routes. Some previously-accepted ambiguous content-types will now be rejected for openai-compat routes to match OpenAI semantics; documented in release notes.

Related: pr-19102, pr-18604 (multipart validation history and earlier limits work).
